PART 2

Three young achievers

Read about the three people, then choose which person each question describes.

Noah Kim, wildlife photographer — Noah began photographing birds in his backyard when he was ten years old. One of his photos was published in a national nature magazine, and he has since won two regional photography awards.

Zara Ahmed, coding tutor — Zara taught herself to code at the age of eleven and built an app that helps students organise their homework. She now runs free coding classes for other children every weekend.

Leo Martins, runner — Leo started running at nine, after being the slowest runner in his class. He now raises money for charity by running marathons, and has completed five of them so far.

PART 3

From robot kits to national finals

Read the article, then choose the correct answer for each question.

Most students go home after school and relax, but Oliver Grant heads straight to the robotics lab. He joined his school's robotics club at the age of eleven, and within two years he had become the team captain.

At first, Oliver only helped assemble simple robot kits, following instructions from an online guide. As he learned more, he started designing his own parts and writing the programs that controlled how the robots moved.

Last year, Oliver's team built a small robot that can carry shopping bags and remind people to take their medicine, designed to help elderly neighbours who live alone. The team entered the robot in a national competition, where they finished in the top three out of more than a hundred schools.

Oliver still spends most of his free time in the robotics lab, and he now helps train the younger members of the club. He clearly has a gift for solving problems and a genuine passion for helping others through technology, and there is little doubt that he will go on to bigger projects in the future.

PART 4

Sofia's journey down the mountain

For each question, choose the correct word for the gap.

Most children reach school by bus or on foot, but Sofia's journey is different. She lives in a small village high in the mountains. The village school had to (19) five years ago because there weren't enough pupils. The nearest school is now down in the valley. Sofia's family keeps a mule, and she can (20) ride it down the mountain path when the weather is dry. A cable car is (21) when snow blocks the path in winter. Every morning, Sofia has to (22) the first cable car down to the valley. She usually returns home by evening, but sometimes she calls home to say she's (23) the night at her aunt's house in the valley instead. "It's a long (24) down the mountain every day," she says, "but I love where I live."
